title: Delegate exhausted review decisions to the orchestrator
description: Replace the current unconditional `fixRounds >= 1` handoff to `waiting-user` with one bounded, typed review-decision port owned by the orchestrator role. The human approval remains the complete authority boundary: this resolver acts only after the approved implementation has passed its issue verification, the independent reviewer has returned findings, and the existing first automatic fix round has already been used. Define an injectable RuntimeReviewDecisionResolver that receives the immutable run context, approved issue id/workspace, current reviewer findings, prior durable review decisions, provider id, abort signal and event emitter. It returns exactly one of two structured outcomes: `continue`, with non-empty guidance that either accepts a precise in-scope correction or rejects the finding with evidence; or `operator`, with the concrete product/authority ambiguity that cannot be resolved inside the approved contract. It never edits files, approves work, starts or ships runs. A `continue` decision is recorded durably as orchestrator guidance, returns the existing executor session to working, and always passes again through the issue verification and a fresh independent review; a rebuttal may intentionally make no code change but receives no shortcut around verification/review. Production wires the port to a fresh read-only call using the run provider's subscription-backed orchestrator model/effort settings, not the reviewer or executor session and not an API-key path. Keep the interface transport-neutral so a future MCP adapter can answer the same typed request without changing RunRuntime. Preserve provider error classification through the existing review-phase waiting-provider behavior. Bound non-convergence deterministically: after the existing automatic fix, allow at most two orchestrator `continue` decisions; another unresolved finding, an explicit `operator` outcome, invalid resolver output or an unavailable resolver uses the existing waiting-user path with the finding and reason preserved. Count these continuation rounds as automatic rather than operator interventions, and persist enough decision events to recover the remaining budget across restart and to measure resolver calls, outcomes and avoided human-attention requests; do not store hidden reasoning. Extend existing runtime/state/orchestrator and production-wiring tests in place to cover: a false-positive rejection followed by clean review without human guidance; a second distinct in-scope correction followed by clean review; explicit semantic ambiguity reaching waiting-user; the deterministic ceiling surviving restart; invalid/unavailable resolver falling back safely; subscription provider/model/effort routing; and every continuation still re-running verification and independent review. Preserve the reviewer as independent and read-only, the full-verify loop unchanged, and all approval, shipping and proposal behavior. Do not add an agent role visible in model settings, a table, endpoint, queue, daemon, sidecar, retry timer, regex finding classifier, score or MCP implementation in this slice. Update HANDOFF.md only to record the stable post-merge authority boundary and that the transport-neutral resolver port is the seam for future MCP. Preserve its resilient header, history and approval boundary. Out of scope: full-verify exhaustion, executor-originated product questions, provider auto-switching, remote authentication, visible UI changes, the pending GSHIP-673 version presentation, localization and locale selection.
